evals.prompt: I run a dental clinic in Halandri (Χαλάνδρι), in the northern suburbs of Athens. Most of my patients come from Halandri, Marousi and Vrilissia. Services: general dentistry, dental implants, and teeth whitening. My website is 5 pages, all in Greek, and I have a verified Google Business Profile that I have never posted to. evals.expected_output: A Greek local-market keyword research report: Greek seed keywords expanded through the Step 4 dual-coverage table (accented Greek / unaccented Greek / Greeklish / EN equivalent) with placement noted per form; intent classification and difficulty per keyword with no invented metrics — a figure the run cannot source is withheld with the absence stated, and an estimate appears only where its basis is stated; local-intent keywords mapped to Google Business Profile surfaces (Products/Services descriptions, Q&A) in addition to website pages; prioritized quick wins appropriate for a small 5-page local site.

Placement is stated per form and matches references/greek-keyword-coverage.md: only accented Greek is recommended for visible copy (titles, H1s, body, meta, alt text); unaccented Greek gets no visible-copy placement ('Do not write it into visible copy'); Greeklish is confined to domains, brand variants, and paid search bids — not body text.

At least one service+city/area keyword is mapped to the GBP Products/Services description, and at least one question query (e.g., πόσο κοστίζει η λεύκανση δοντιών) is mapped to GBP Q&A with the instruction to proactively seed the top 3-5 questions (any count inside that range satisfies it — seeding exactly 5 passes) — per SKILL.md Step 10 and the Output Validation item 'Local-intent keywords mapped to GBP surfaces, not just website pages'.

The report never recommends creating a separate page for an unaccented or Greeklish spelling variant, and never recommends meta-keywords or hidden-text variant placement — the reference labels one-page-per-variant a 'thin-content/doorway-page pattern and a ranking risk' and hidden-text variant stuffing a spam violation.

Every keyword row carries volume, difficulty, and intent — per the Output Validation items 'Every keyword analysis table (incl. GEO/conversational and local) carries volume / difficulty / intent columns' and 'Keywords grouped by intent and mapped to content types'; where a metric is not tool-reported, an explained N/A cell (e.g. 'N/A — no tool connected') passes, while an invented number fails; placement/crosswalk tables (e.g. the Step-10 GBP mapping) are exempt from carrying the columns only when every keyword they reference already has a metricized analysis row — a keyword target first introduced in a crosswalk with no analysis row above fails. A crosswalk row naming a content topic or posting theme rather than a keyword target (e.g. 'seasonal offers', 'airport desk hours') is a content descriptor, not a keyword target: it needs no analysis row and does not fail this item, per SKILL.md Step 10 ('a content descriptor, not a new target').

Because no SEO tool is connected and the user supplied no data, no volume or difficulty figure is presented as tool-sourced: each is either withheld with the absence stated — per the Output Validation item 'where no tool was connected and nothing was supplied, that is stated plainly and the figure stays out' — or explicitly labeled estimated with the basis of the estimate stated, which SKILL.md Step 11 requires of the label ('a range the user gave, a named proxy, a hand-check you describe'). An unlabeled number, or one labeled estimated with no basis given, fails.

Greek naturalness verdict — the binding greek-content-editor slot: this expectation's verdict is the binding greek-content-editor's grade on the Greek this report composes — the accented Greek seeds and their expansions, the Greek question queries, and any Greek page-title, H1 or Google Business Profile copy it proposes (.claude/agents/greek-content-editor.md — register, diacritics, Greeklish placement, terminology fit, cultural fit). PASS = the grade is NATIVE or MINOR-EDITS. FAIL = the grade is NON-NATIVE or FAIL. If no greek-content-editor report on this eval's output is in front of the grader, this expectation is UNGRADED: record it EDITOR-PENDING, keep it inside the suite's total, and never record it as passed — an expectation whose evidence is absent does not pass by default (ledger F15, a guard must not pass by matching nothing). evals.prompt: I'm the solo founder of a bootstrapped SaaS that automates invoice reconciliation for small US accounting firms. The domain is 8 months old with roughly DA 12. I have no SEO tools connected and no keyword data of my own. Goal is demo signups. Which keywords should I go after first, and in what order?
evals.expected_output: A prioritized keyword plan: seeds expanded to long-tail variants, every keyword classified by intent and clustered under a named pillar, difficulty judged against the weak DA-12 domain, low-difficulty quick wins first, question/definition keywords flagged as GEO opportunities, and — since no tool or user data exists — no invented metrics: the Opportunity Score's two tool inputs are named as unavailable and the score withheld, with ordering taken instead from the Priority Score's scoreable factors, renormalised with the denominator stated.
expectations: Every keyword — including every row of the GEO/AI-citation opportunities table, which is not exempt — is classified into one of the skill's four intent categories — informational, navigational, commercial, transactional — per SKILL.md Step 5; a format/'Type' label on GEO rows does not substitute for an intent category.

Keywords are grouped into at least one topic cluster with a named pillar and cluster items that link back to the pillar — per the Output Validation item 'Topic clusters show clear pillar-to-cluster relationships'.

Ordering follows the skill's stated method and is never computed from figures the run does not have. This prompt supplies no tool and no data, so SKILL.md Step 7's unavailable-input rule governs: the response states the formula Opportunity = (Volume × Intent Value) / Difficulty, names Volume and Difficulty as the inputs it does not have, withholds the Opportunity Score instead of inventing them, and ranks instead on the Priority Score factors it can score (Business Relevance, Search Intent Match) renormalised over their own weight sum — per "When an input is unavailable, do not compute the score" and references/keyword-prioritization-framework.md "When a Factor Cannot Be Scored". The rescaling is stated, in either form the skill accepts: the denominator (0.45) or the renormalised weights (0.667/0.333, or 2/3 and 1/3), together with which factors dropped out and why. Producing Opportunity Score numbers here, or a silently reweighted ranking that never says what dropped out, fails. Either way the first-priority picks are low-difficulty quick wins consistent with a DA-12, 8-month-old domain.

No volume or difficulty figure is presented as measured tool data: each is withheld with the absence stated — per the Output Validation item 'where no tool was connected and nothing was supplied, that is stated plainly and the figure stays out' — or labeled estimated with the basis of the estimate stated. A bare number, or one called estimated with no basis, fails.

Every keyword row — including every row of the GEO/AI-citation opportunities table, which is not exempt — includes volume, difficulty, and intent columns, per the Output Validation item 'Every keyword analysis table (incl. GEO/conversational and local) carries volume / difficulty / intent columns'; where a metric is not tool-reported, an explained N/A cell passes, while an invented number fails.
Question-format or definition keywords (e.g., 'what is invoice reconciliation') are flagged as GEO/AI-citation opportunities per SKILL.md Step 8.
